clue.text: Moving against him, the writer succeeded in competition honouring Poseidon

indicators.note: letters that are moving do not stay where they were put, so AGAINST HIM is rearranged

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to himself as ME
s. = succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An athlete wins a contest held for the sea god, beating a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Only AGAINST HIM is mixed; ME and S are added whole at the end. 'Moving against him' reads as a wrestler's tactic, and 'succeeded in competition' as winning.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the Isthmian Games were the ancient Greek festival held at Corinth in Poseidon's honour.

clue.text: Headless maggot snaffled by young canary

indicators.note: a word with no head has lost its first letter
to snaffle is to grab and keep, so the young one holds the maggot inside itself

parts.note: an infant is a young child; it wraps round the next piece
a maggot is a WORM; headless, (W)ORM

explanation.surface: A young songbird gobbles up a grub it has half-eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canary' sits at the end looking like a bird to match the maggot, but in slang a canary is someone who sings to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a canary 'sings', telling the police what they know, which is what an informant does.

clue.text: Catching rook, Pooh's feline friend makes start

indicators.note: what catches something holds it, so the friend's name closes round the rook

parts.note: Tigger, the tiger in Winnie-the-Pooh; wraps round the R

explanation.surface: Tigger pounces on a bird, which gives it a start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes start' reads as 'gives a fright', but 'start' is a verb, set going, and 'makes' only links it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: setting off an event, as a gun's trigger sets off a shot.

clue.text: With which condition one doesn't normally feel great?

definitions.text: With which condition one doesn't normally feel great?

parts.note: the surface wants an illness that leaves you under the weather
read literally: a condition in which you feel great, mighty, as normal people don't

explanation.surface: A question about an illness that stops you feeling well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feel great' reads as 'feel healthy'; take it literally: this is the condition of feeling great, that is grand and all-powerful, which normal people do not.
explanation.definitionFit: Megalomania is the delusion of one's own greatness, so its sufferer abnormally feels great in the grand sense.

clue.text: Author having four sisters in family occupying rural cottage

definitions.text: Author having four sisters in family

indicators.note: the answer occupies, lives inside, the words that follow

explanation.surface: A writer from a big family living in a country cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: The four sisters are the March girls of Little Women; the author herself was one of four sisters too.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women, about the four March sisters.

clue.text: Lovely keyboard instrument in county once

explanation.surface: A beautiful organ found somewhere in the countryside long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan was a county of south Wales, split up in 1974, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A former county: Glamorgan was abolished as a single county in the 1974 reorganisation.

clue.text: Bloom reserving different name for female who knows best

indicators.note: to reserve something is to keep it in hand, so the bloom holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to bloom is to mature, come into full flower; it wraps round what follows

explanation.surface: A flower kept back under a different label for a know-all woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloom' is a verb here, not a flower. The definition leans on the saying 'Mother Nature knows best'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: nature personified as a wise woman, and proverbially she knows best.

clue.text: Grass skirts with jumper in an estuary

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so the grass goes round WITH

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, so a grass is one who shops people; it wraps round AND

explanation.surface: A grass skirt worn with a sweater at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass skirts' and 'jumper' paint a wardrobe. In British slang a grass is an informer, and the jumper is a small leaping crustacean.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by habit: these tiny crustaceans leap about on sandy shores and estuary mud.

clue.text: Negotiator in attempt to gamble? Small point

parts.note: have a go = make an attempt

explanation.surface: A deal-maker taking a small punt.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and full stop split the clue into two scraps, but it is one long chain of pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a go-between carries terms back and forth between two parties, as a negotiator does.

clue.text: Good hill climbing finds poet's cave

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means going upwards, so the hill is read from the bottom

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A walker going up a fine hill comes across a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' warns that the answer is a literary word, a short form of grotto.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word: poets shorten grotto to grot, hence 'poet's'.

clue.text: Attend a match on sparsely settled land, or prevaricate?

parts.note: to attend is to BE AT
a boxing bout is a match
the bush is the Australian outback

explanation.surface: Going to a game out in the wilds, or dodging the question.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is split into new words: BE AT A BOUT, (on) THE BUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to beat about the bush is to avoid coming to the point.

clue.text: Follower crossing Republican's path

indicators.note: to cross something is to go across it, here spanning it so the letter sits inside

parts.note: a tail is someone following you; it wraps round R

explanation.surface: A supporter getting in a Republican politician's way.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rough track through country is both.

clue.text: Nobleman with award for organ piece?

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour

explanation.surface: An aristocrat receives a prize for an organ composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ piece' suggests music; the organ is the ear and the piece a part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: the ear is an organ of the body and the lobe is a piece of it.

clue.text: Cold war aftermath? Tough to secure outright victory on retreating!

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the tough holds the victory inside
what retreats goes backwards, so ON's letters are reversed

parts.note: a nut, as in 'hard nut', is a tough guy; wraps round the victory
a clear win is an outright one

explanation.surface: A call to win the Cold War outright without giving ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold war' looks like the US-Soviet stand-off; the question mark flags a pun, since after a nuclear war the world would literally turn cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on 'cold war': the predicted global chill after nuclear war is a literally cold aftermath of war.

clue.text: Cast of Brief Encounter

definitions.meaning: not the film but a short affair

explanation.surface: The actors in the 1945 film Brief Encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make you think of the film and its cast; lower-case, a brief encounter is a short affair, a FLING, and to fling is to cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to throw something, and a short-lived romance.

clue.text: Talk to an eccentric old goat periodically in city

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre, odd

parts.note: o = old; joins TO AN in the mix to give TANOO

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter of goat

explanation.surface: Chatting to a batty old goat now and then somewhere in town.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'eccentric old goat' looks like one character, but 'eccentric' is working on the words either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Chattanooga is a city in Tennessee.

clue.text: Goldfinger having sport among spooks from the East

indicators.note: something among others sits in their midst, so the sport goes inside the spooks
in an across entry the east is the right-hand end, so read from there, right to left

parts.note: spooks are spies; the CIA is the US spy agency; it wraps round RU

explanation.surface: The Bond villain playing a game among Eastern spies.
explanation.walkthrough: CI(RU)A is built first, then the whole thing is read backwards. Goldfinger's first name in the Bond novel means 'of gold'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by name: Auric is the Bond villain Goldfinger's first name, and the word itself means golden.

clue.text: Fit pair to be worn by Latvian hunchback

parts.note: to rig out is to fit out, equip

indicators.note: what a person wears goes round them, so the pair sits either side of the Latvian

parts.note: in cricket a pair is two ducks, two noughts in one match; they go round LETT

explanation.surface: Fitting a Latvian with a pair of something to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair' is cricket slang: out for nought in both innings, two O's. The hunchback is the jester of Verdi's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Verdi's Rigoletto is a hunchbacked court jester.

clue.text: Nymph consorting with Zeus evoked memory

definitions.meaning: the mountain nymph who kept Hera chattering while Zeus had his affairs
a trace of the past called back to mind

explanation.surface: A nymph with Zeus brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence with 'evoked' as its verb; it is two separate definitions side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the nymph of Greek myth, and a noun for a reminder that recalls something earlier.

clue.text: Name that is embracing artistic work?

definitions.text: Name that is embracing artistic work?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms

parts.note: i.e. = that is; wraps round OP

explanation.surface: A question about a name tied to art.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the name of a Muse, one who embraces artistic work.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: Calliope, Muse of epic poetry, is a name standing for artistic inspiration.

clue.text: Medic with a touring car in Caribbean island

indicators.note: a tour goes round a place

parts.note: A added after DOC; DOCA then wraps round MINI
the Mini is a British car

explanation.surface: A doctor taking a road trip around a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A touring car' looks like one thing, a kind of car; it is 'a' going round the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Dominica is an island nation in the eastern Caribbean.

clue.text: Built with steeply angled sides, A&E accommodates female sheep

indicators.note: to accommodate is to find room for, so A&E takes the sheep inside

parts.note: A and E, with the next two pieces between them

explanation.surface: A hospital casualty ward takes in a sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female sheep' looks like a ewe, but 'female' and 'sheep' are separate pieces, the second a ram. A&E is a British hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: an A-frame building has steep sides meeting at the top like the letter A.

clue.text: Troublemaker co-partner at Vogue sacked

indicators.note: a sacked city is plundered and wrecked, its contents scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troublesome business partner fired from the fashion magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' reads as fired from a job; here it means ravaged, which rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an agent provocateur is planted to stir up trouble or incite crime.

clue.text: Pioneering MP Nancy — minister powerless!

indicators.note: without power, and P is the abbreviation for power, so the P goes

parts.note: a pastor is a minister of religion; minus P

explanation.surface: A trailblazing MP turns out to be a minister without clout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests government; here it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Nancy Astor was the first woman to take her seat in the House of Commons.

clue.text: Enigmatic librarian! Run to me! Hippasus' discovery revealed?

indicators.note: an enigma is a puzzle, so these letters are puzzled into a new order

explanation.surface: A mysterious librarian is urged to come quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Hippasus, a follower of Pythagoras, is said to have been drowned for revealing that the square root of 2 cannot be a fraction, which is why 'revealed' is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by history: Hippasus is credited with proving that some numbers cannot be written as fractions.

clue.text: Game's instruction given to those who'd dump illegally?

definitions.meaning: an informal form of cricket where the batter must run after every hit

definitions.text: instruction given to those who'd dump illegally?
definitions.meaning: dump your rubbish, then make off

explanation.surface: Advice for fly-tippers, framed as the rules of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain to tip is to dump rubbish, and illegal dumping is fly-tipping. Tip-and-run cricket makes the batter run whenever the ball is hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a cricket game, and literally what a fly-tipper does.

clue.text: What should get one well? Old man receives a card

parts.note: pa = father, old man; wraps round what follows

explanation.surface: An elderly father is handed a get-well card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A card' after 'get one well' suggests a get-well card; read it as AN ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a panacea is a cure-all, supposed to make anyone well.

clue.text: Modernist initially stranded in bog pushed back

indicators.note: at the start, so only the first letter of stranded is used
the letter is put in, inside, the bog

parts.note: bog is British slang for toilet; reversed, TELIOT holds the S

indicators.note: something pushed back is sent backwards, so the bog's letters are reversed

explanation.surface: A modern artist trapped in a marsh and forced to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' reads as marshland; in British slang it is a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the author of The Waste Land was a leading modernist poet.

clue.text: Tribesperson expresses disapproval with India

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
I = India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A tribal member frowns on India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expresses disapproval' is a verb phrase, and it gives the verb form, with its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi.

clue.text: Social networker using rather cute, brief epithet, say

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an epithet is one kind of term; brief, TER

explanation.surface: Someone online choosing a sweet, short nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the epithet as just one example of a TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone who posts on Twitter is a user of a social network.

clue.text: Semite near Moroccan location brought round by hospital in city

indicators.note: something brought round is turned to face the other way, so the letters are reversed

explanation.surface: An Arab near Rabat is taken back to a city hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers the whole chain, not just the hospital, so the pieces come out in the opposite order.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Santa Barbara is a city on the California coast.

clue.text: Sign refurbished with lilac tint becomes brilliant

indicators.note: a thing refurbished is done up afresh, so the letters are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A shop sign repainted in lilac looks dazzling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'brilliant' a paint colour; it is the definition, meaning sparkling or witty.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean sparkling, dazzlingly clever.

clue.text: Secured loan without interest outside bank

indicators.note: the first piece stands outside the second, so it goes round it

parts.note: bored = lacking interest; wraps round ROW
a bank of seats or keys is a row

explanation.surface: An interest-free loan arranged from a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' and 'bank' shout finance, but 'without interest' means BORED and the bank is a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb phrase in the past: having secured a loan of something is having borrowed it.

clue.text: One such as Caiaphas: when drunk he is right to keep quiet

indicators.note: drunk words stagger, so their letters come out in a new order
to keep something is to hold it

parts.note: p = piano, quiet; kept inside the fodder

explanation.surface: A drunken man insists he's right while being told to hush.
explanation.walkthrough: Caiaphas presided at the trial of Jesus in the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Caiaphas held the office of high priest of the Temple in Jerusalem.

clue.text: Shopper in Cardiff perhaps eating fresh brie for snack

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so the cheese goes inside the rat
something fresh is made new, so the letters of brie are rearranged

parts.note: a rat is an informer, a shopper; one from Cardiff is Welsh
BRIE rearranged, eaten by the rat

explanation.surface: A Cardiff shopper nibbling brie for a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' looks like someone at the shops; it is someone who shops others, a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: cheese melted on toast is a classic British snack.

clue.text: Maybe Van Gogh's content with chronicle being scandalous?

parts.note: Van Gogh's first name, VINCENT, with only its inside letters kept

explanation.surface: Speculation that Van Gogh's letters might be shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' tells you Van Gogh is only an example of someone with that first name.

clue.text: On the drink heading to North Country

indicators.note: north is up the page, so in a down entry the letters are read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone drinking while travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the drink' sounds like being drunk; it is two pieces, turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Niger is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Carriage reserved for small charge?

parts.note: the surface wants a booked railway carriage
not a cheap fare: the charge is a baby in someone's care

explanation.surface: A train carriage booked at a low fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' and 'small charge' suggest a cheap reserved seat on a train; the charge is a child in one's care, and the carriage is its pram.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: a pram is a carriage kept for a small person in one's charge.

clue.text: Be in right gear, good enough to enter lot — centre includes parking

indicators.note: what includes something holds it within

parts.note: the heart is the centre; wraps round P

explanation.surface: A car park worth entering, with parking in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The car-park picture of 'lot', 'centre' and 'parking' hides three separate pieces; 'right gear' is clothes, not a car's gearbox.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to look the part is to be dressed right for a role.

clue.text: Evidence no longer in circulation wasted on tabloids

explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer in circulation' sounds like a withdrawn newspaper; it belongs to the definition, as blood that has left the circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: forensic evidence made of blood that is no longer circulating in the body.

clue.text: At first they were all nervy — finally showing pluck

indicators.note: at the start, so the first letter of each of the next words

parts.note: They Were All Nervy: first letters

indicators.note: at the end, so the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Everyone was on edge but in the end showed courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' reads as courage, which suits the nerves; it is the verb for sounding a string.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: plucking a string makes it sound with a sharp ring.

clue.text: Pasta strings, however many? Thousands!

parts.note: n is the algebraic any number

explanation.surface: How many strands of spaghetti? Loads.
explanation.walkthrough: The question and exclamation look like a conversation; they are two pieces, a maths symbol and a slang word for lots.

clue.text: Man's woman returned chart

explanation.surface: A man's partner came back with a map.

explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a histogram is a kind of bar chart showing frequencies.

clue.text: Dish with Castro regularly causing tricky problem

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of Castro

explanation.surface: Serving a stew to Castro stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Castro is only there for his letters. A hotpot is a British stew topped with sliced potato and baked slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an issue too awkward to keep, like a potato too hot to handle.

clue.text: Boring people make this missile after bomb

the missile goes after the bomb

explanation.surface: Dull people build a weapon on top of a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring people' are not dull; they bore, drilling into the ground.

clue.text: Conservative turncoat in terribly miserable old political group

parts.note: MISERABLE OLD rearranged; it holds C RAT

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old political group' looks like the definition, but 'old' belongs to the anagram.

clue.text: Unwell when engaged by Scottish bank, touch-type?

clue.text: Image of body shown in court, endlessly deficient

clue.text: Close the gap almost filled with eastern plant extract

clue.text: Hostess to an extent in short dress

clue.text: Prickly plant in a container like this

explanation.surface: A spiny plant potted up like so.

clue.text: Band in hotel criminal society guards

clue.text: Addict taken in because reoffending

clue.text: Dramatic works from poetaster to be rewritten

clue.text: Current hopelessness unending in White House

clue.text: Forward striking idiot with supporters having invaded

clue.text: Conservationists in state bound to be heard
